events.operator: Yanbu Aramco Sinopec Refining Co. (Aramco / Sinopec JV)
events.summary: The Saudi energy ministry said an attack on YASREF facilities led to a temporary reduction in the refinery's production. It was the only site in the 20 March 2022 wave for which an output effect was officially stated.
events.effect: Ministry: the attack "led to a temporary reduction in the refinery's production, which will be compensated for from the inventory." No volume or duration given.
events.threshold_basis: Clause 1: official statement of a reduction in refinery throughput following an attack.

recovery.evidence: Ministry said the reduction "will be compensated for from the inventory". This is a supply-continuity statement, not evidence of a refinery restart; no restart date or return-to-normal statement was found.

events.facility_name: Juaymah NGL facility / LPG export terminal
events.summary: Aramco said a small segment of the propane/butane delivery system at Juaymah was structurally damaged on 23 February 2026, halted LPG exports from the site and declared force majeure on shipments.
events.effect: LPG export loadings from Juaymah halted; force majeure declared. Argus (15 Sep 2026): "No LPG cargoes have left Ras Tanura following an accident at the facility on 23 February."
events.threshold_basis: Clause 2: operator-confirmed suspension of energy (LPG) export loadings.

recovery.evidence: No confirmed resumption found. Bloomberg-sourced reports (late April) said suspension extended through May; OPIS reported July cargoes cancelled; Argus (15 Sep 2026) said some participants EXPECTED September loadings because Aramco issued September acceptances - an expectation, not observed loadings.

events.summary: Aramco shut the Ras Tanura refinery as a precaution while assessing damage after an attack; a limited fire was reported. The refinery later restarted.
events.effect: Refinery shut down (energy ministry statement via state news agency, as reported by Bloomberg): shut "as a precaution while assessing damage."
events.threshold_basis: Clause 1: refinery shut down after an attack, per official statement.

capacity_affected.source_says: Bloomberg/World Oil: the 550,000 b/d refinery was shut (full shutdown, so nameplate = affected throughput).

recovery.evidence: Restart reported; operating rate NOT stated. Dates conflict: Dow Jones headline 10 Mar ('Saudi Aramco Says Ras Tanura Refinery Restarts'); industry monitor IIR via Iran International: restarted 13 Mar; The National (12 Apr): 'closed for 16 days before restarting'. Kind set to service_restored rather than full_restart because throughput after restart is unreported.

events.summary: TotalEnergies said incidents on the night of 7-8 April damaged units at SATORP and the refinery was shut as a safety precaution; undamaged units restarted on 14 April.
events.effect: Full shutdown 8-14 April; then operation at 230,000 b/d (TotalEnergies). TotalEnergies CEO (June): running at about 70%.
events.threshold_basis: Clause 1: operator-confirmed refinery shutdown and sustained throughput cut.

capacity_affected.source_says: TotalEnergies: since 14 April the refinery 'has been operating at a capacity of 230,000 b/d' - i.e. roughly half of the 460,000 b/d plant offline after the partial restart.

recovery.evidence: TotalEnergies: undamaged units restarted; operating at 230,000 b/d since 14 April. CEO Pouyanne (to French National Assembly, reported 18 Jun 2026): about 70% capacity; full repair probably not before early 2027 (an operator ESTIMATE, not an observation).

events.summary: Industry monitor IIR reported that Aramco shut the Jazan refinery on 27 July 2026 after an attack claimed by Yemen's Houthis. After a fire at a refinery facility on 9 August, which the energy ministry said was extinguished, IIR reported the restart postponed to 30 August.
events.effect: Refinery shut from 27 July 2026; planned restart moved from 15 August to 30 August.
events.threshold_basis: Refinery shut down, with the effect reported by an industry monitor.

recovery.evidence: No report confirming a restart was found in searches on 30 October 2026; the last report read gave a target of 30 August 2026.

events.summary: Shipping sources said crude loadings at Yanbu were suspended after the East-West pipeline was shut on 11 September. Loadings had not resumed by 24 September but had resumed before 1 October.
events.effect: Crude export loadings suspended (Reuters shipping sources, reported 15 Sep; Aramco declined comment).
events.threshold_basis: Clause 2: reported suspension of crude export loadings.

recovery.evidence: Marine Insight (3 Oct 2026) says the 1 Oct incident came 'days after' Yanbu loadings resumed following the pipeline restart; Baird Maritime lists a 29 Sep headline that Yanbu crude flows resumed (not opened). Exact resumption date not verified.

events.summary: The energy ministry said the East-West crude pipeline was shut 'as a precautionary measure' after multiple attacks. Reuters sources later said it restarted on 22 September, with full capacity possibly six weeks or more away.
events.effect: Pipeline shut down (ministry). Knock-on: crude loadings at Yanbu suspended (see sa-2026-09-yanbu-loadings-suspended).
events.threshold_basis: Clause 3: official statement that a crude trunk pipeline was shut down.

recovery.evidence: Reuters (three sources): pipeline restarted on 22 Sep; may take six weeks or more to reach full capacity. Bloomberg source (16 Sep): aim to restore about half of capacity 'within days', full in about six weeks (ESTIMATE). An ARY News item says Aramco 'completely restarted' it at full capacity, but its dates are internally inconsistent - not relied on.
